gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'We're moving to Lisbon,' they announced. They announced that they ___ to Lisbon.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous backshifts to past continuous: are moving → were moving.

gaps.sentence: "Do not touch the wire!" — She warned me ___ the wire.
gaps.explanation: 'Warn somebody not to do' — 'not' comes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: 'I've lost my keys,' she admitted. She admitted that she ___ her keys.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: have lost → had lost.

gaps.sentence: They ___ us that the museum had closed early.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody (that)... — 'told' needs the direct personal object 'us'; 'said' cannot take it.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
"Can you help me?" — She asked ___ help her.
'When did the ancient city fall?' we asked the guide. We asked the guide when the ancient city ___.
gaps.explanation: did...fall → had fallen: the auxiliary 'did' disappears and the verb backshifts.
